chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهَ وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ ابْنَا نَصِيرٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى، عَنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ، عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, the sons of Nusayr, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abi Usama who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ رَجُلٌ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: أُؤَخِّرُ الْمَغْرِبَ حَتَّى تَسْتَبِينَ النُّجُومُ؟ قَالَ: فَقَالَ: خَطَّابِيَّةٌ، إِنَّ جِبْرِيلَ أَنْزَلَهَا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ حِينَ سَقَطَ الْقُرْصُ

translations.en: A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Should I postpone the Maghrib prayer until the stars become visible? He (peace be upon him) said: [It is the view of the] Khattabiyya! Verily, Jibrail brought it [i.e., the ruling/time] to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when the disk [of the sun] disappeared.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the common misconception of waiting for star visibility by identifying it as the view of the Khattabiyya, affirming that Maghrib time commences immediately upon the disappearance of the sun's disk. This ruling is grounded in the divine revelation received by the Prophet through Jibrail, emphasizing the precision of the celestial signs as originally prescribed. The distinction highlights the importance of adhering to the specific moment of sunset rather than the subsequent astronomical phenomena often used in later calculations.
en.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer begin according to Shia hadith?

key_terms.النُّجُوم: Stars (used here to denote a later time for prayer)
key_terms.خَطَّابِيَّةٌ: Khattabiyya (a reference to a specific group or school of thought regarding prayer times)
key_terms.الْقُرْص: The disk (referring to the sun's disk)
